phrases.latin: pater eam lēniter conjiciēbat, Theodōrus manibus excipiēbat, aut, sī ēlāpsa erat, pede ad patrem pulsābat
phrases.english: Dad tossed it gently, Theo caught it in his hands or, if it slipped, kicked it back to Dad

phrases.latin: Ibi follem, quem puerī quīdam pede pulsābant, ad sē volūtum Theodōrus ambābus manibus ad eōs conjēcit.
phrases.english: There some boys were kicking a ball; when it rolled to him Theo threw it back to them with both hands.
phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 44, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
